The closest match to “identifying clusters by removing odd ones out using a few starting markers” is Seed-Guided Semi-Supervised Clustering by A-Contrario Anomaly Detection. It uses a seed-guided, “clustering-by-exclusion” mechanism where clusters are defined as maximal subsets containing no anomalies under an a-contrario null hypothesis, and an iterative process admits non-anomalous points to expand groups initialized from robust cluster medians. It also claims that few seeds per cluster (as few as 10–30) can work well without manual parameter tuning, which aligns with the “few starting markers” aspect. [1]

Other papers here don’t directly focus on “removing odd ones out” with seed markers. Persistent Multiscale Density-based Clustering proposes a density-based method that avoids manual hyperparameter selection via persistence-based cluster selection, but it’s not seed-guided. [4]
